lateral_flank_blob_constellation.centroid_triangulation: Three distinct horizontal rows of high-luminance circular blobs are visible. The medial row aligns with the secondary carina, with spots spaced approximately two diameters apart. Lower rows show increasing spatial variance and decreased intensity toward the ventral margin.
lateral_flank_blob_constellation.stripe_intersections: Faint vertical bands of elevated pixel intensity intersect the horizontal carinae, creating a coarse grid where the high-luminance blobs serve as nodal points.

carinae_gradient_vectors.ridge_trajectory: Three prominent horizontal carinae are visible. The superior ridge exhibits a sharp luminance gradient, transitioning from high-intensity white light on the dorsal edge to a deep shadowed ventral valley, running parallel to the shark's longitudinal axis until truncated by a posterior lesion.

dorsal_fin_surface_patterning.internal_spot_density: The first dorsal fin contains approximately five discrete high-luminance blobs concentrated near the posterior margin. The second dorsal fin shows a lower density of more diffuse, low-contrast patches.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A major V-shaped indentation or healed tissue loss is present on the dorsal ridge between the first and second dorsal fins. A large, dark, ovoid mass (likely a remora or large parasitic attachment) is situated immediately posterior to the base of the first dorsal fin.
other_distinctive_markers: Multiple small, mobile silhouettes of high-contrast difference are visible along the ventral periphery, consistent with commensal pilot fish or remoras.
